headline: Mistakes People Make Repairing Wood Fences
articleBody: It’s tempting to jump in and fix a wobbly fence yourself, but some common missteps can turn a simple repair into a bigger headache. One frequent mistake is only replacing the visible damaged board without checking the underlying posts. Often, post rot is the real culprit, and simply swapping out a picket won't solve the long-term problem. Always inspect the posts thoroughly. Another blunder is setting new boards on a failing frame. If the rails or supporting structure are compromised, new pickets will soon follow suit. Make sure the entire framework is sturdy before reattaching anything. Using incompatible fasteners is also a common issue; for instance, using nails that aren't weather-resistant will lead to rust streaks and weakening over time. Always match your hardware to the environment and wood type. And perhaps one of the biggest oversights is ignoring the drainage and soil contact that caused the damage in the first place. If the bottom of your fence is consistently sitting in water, new wood will just rot again. Addressing the source of moisture is crucial for a lasting repair. If you're finding that the damage is more extensive than just a loose picket, or if you're unsure about the structural integrity, it's a good idea to reach out to a professional.
